name: Jiani (Elva) He
headline: Data Science Consultant · Independent Researcher

stats.label: Years in data center supply chains

bio: Jiani (Elva) He is a data scientist and independent researcher focused on AI-assisted reverse logistics: using information about returned assets to support inspection, recovery, and disposition decisions. A Data Science Consultant at Accenture, Jiani works on planning analytics for a technology client’s data center supply chains. Jiani proposed the core research idea and methodological framework for SSADS, a first-author paper at AIBThings 2026, and is a co-first author of DACRI at ICECCME 2026. Jiani’s six 2026 conference papers also span forecasting, planning value, early warning, and AI assurance. The conferences have concluded; proceedings are forthcoming. Jiani holds an MS in Business Analytics from MIT and a BS in Industrial Engineering from Purdue.

streams.label: Reverse logistics
streams.name: AI-Assisted Reverse Logistics
streams.question: How can unstructured signals guide inspection and recovery when labor is scarce?
streams.motivation: Returned assets arrive with uncertain condition and free-text notes. Choosing how deeply to inspect each one, and whether it goes to reuse, resale, recycling, or disposal, is a resource-allocation problem under partial information.
streams.practice: Tracking reverse-logistics cycle times and guiding disposition decisions for retired data center hardware
streams.title: A second life for returned hardware
streams.short: In SSADS, we treat return notes as imperfect evidence for deciding how much inspection to allocate before choosing a recovery route.
streams.evidence: Three synthetic reverse-logistics scenarios: IT decommissioning, aircraft maintenance, and consumer-electronics returns.

streams.label: Decision support & trustworthy AI
streams.name: Causal Decision Support & Trustworthy AI
streams.question: Which action should come next, and when can the evidence behind it be trusted?
streams.motivation: Detecting a disruption is not the same as knowing which intervention recovers the most value. Good decisions need causal evidence and explicit costs and delays. AI-enabled decisions also need provenance that people can review before deployment.
streams.practice: Rebalancing inventory across sites and standardizing enterprise LLM workflows
streams.title: Which action is worth taking?
streams.short: In DACRI, we compare interventions under explicit costs, delays, and incomplete information. Related work examines the policy and provenance evidence needed to qualify an LLM-routing system for deployment.
streams.evidence: Controlled supply-chain simulations with causal ground truth; a separate study of deployment assurance for LLM request routing.

streams.label: Forecasting & planning
streams.name: Forecasting & Planning Value
streams.question: When do better predictions actually produce better plans?
streams.motivation: A forecast can score well on point accuracy and still move sharply between adjacent time steps. A planning tool also needs to be evaluated through the cost and feasibility of the plans it produces.
streams.practice: Analyzing demand, stock targets, and shortages across a data center supply network
streams.title: Forecasts planners can act on
streams.short: With collaborators, I study the trade-off between forecast accuracy and stability, early warning for delivery risk, and the operational value of added planning capabilities.
streams.evidence: Retail-demand forecasting experiments; forecast-to-plan replay on Favorita, M5, and Walmart data; separate work on late-delivery risk.

publications.title: Semantic Signal-Assisted Inspection and Recovery Allocation in Reverse Logistics
publications.venue: 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things (AIBThings 2026)
publications.summary: Uses semantic signals in return notes to guide inspection depth and recovery allocation when asset condition is uncertain and inspection labor is limited. Evaluated in three synthetic reverse-logistics scenarios.
publications.short: Semantic-signal inspection and recovery allocation (first author)

publications.title: DACRI: Decision-Aware Causal Intervention Ranking for Critical Supply Chains
publications.venue: International Conference on Electrical, Computer, Communications and Mechatronics Engineering (ICECCME 2026) · 15–17 October 2026 · Bali, Indonesia
publications.summary: Ranks supply-chain interventions by recoverable net value, using a controlled synthetic benchmark with causal ground truth and explicit intervention costs, delays, and uncertainty. Identifies when adaptive ranking pays off and when simpler structural policies remain preferable.
publications.short: DACRI: decision-aware causal intervention ranking (co-first author)

publications.title: When Does an Added Planning Capability Create Operational Value? An Observable Evidence Standard
publications.venue: 3rd World Congress on Industrial Engineering and Operations Management · Irvine, California
publications.summary: An observable evidence standard for deciding whether an added planning capability changes executed plans and improves operational outcomes, evaluated through forecast-to-plan replay on retail datasets.
publications.short: Observable evidence standard for planning capabilities

publications.title: From Weak Signals to Supply Chain Reliability Risk: A Feedback-Driven Risk Accumulation Framework for Late-Delivery Prediction, Early Warning, and Risk Prioritization
publications.venue: 3rd World Congress on Industrial Engineering and Operations Management · Irvine, California
publications.summary: A leakage-controlled, feedback-driven risk-accumulation framework that turns weak operational signals into late-delivery predictions, early warnings, and cost-sensitive risk prioritization.
publications.short: Late-delivery risk prediction and early warning

publications.title: Accuracy-Preserving Stability Regularization for Large-Scale Retail Demand Forecasting
publications.summary: Training-time regularization that reduces movement between adjacent time steps within a retail-demand forecast while preserving point accuracy, evaluated on selected M5 series at multiple scales.

publications.title: Policy-Bounded, Provenance-Aware Deployment Assurance for LLM Request Routing
publications.summary: Studies how policy boundaries, provenance, and evidence identity determine whether an LLM request-routing package is qualified for deployment and for later updates.
publications.short: Deployment assurance for LLM request routing

importance.cet_intro: The U.S. Critical and Emerging Technologies (CET) List identifies technology areas of national-security importance. Its August 2026 update, published as Appendix A of the White House National Security Science and Technology Strategy, narrows the list to 14 areas. My work relates to two of them.

cet_rows.detail: AI for planning and decision making, AI assurance and assessment, and trustworthy deployment of large language models, all named as AI subfields in the February 2024 list.
Data center hardware is built on semiconductors and microelectronics. For five years I have planned, rebalanced, and recovered that hardware across a technology client’s data center supply chain.

philosophy.intro: Some of the most useful things I know, I learned from operations. Here are a few stories that shape how I work and live.

stories.title: Why I chose optimization
text: I’m bothered by how much useful material goes to waste.

A returned component may still have a useful life ahead of it. Deciding whether to put it back into inventory, remarket it, or scrap it is a question of evidence, condition, and allocation. That’s why I chose operations research and optimization.

stories.title: A mission for the long term
text: I care about long-term thinking. Before committing to something, I want to know what mission it serves and what belief will sustain the effort.
In this work, that belief is straightforward: we can make better use of the resources we already have.

stories.title: Always learning
text: Graduating didn’t end school for me. It just ended the grades.
Since then I’ve learned investing, read widely, picked up meditation, and tried all kinds of sports. I want to grow as a whole person, not only as a professional.

stories.title: Someone people can talk to
text: When people around me are stuck, they often come to talk. I’m energetic, and I hope I’m warm.
Watching someone leave a conversation a little lighter than they came in is one of my favorite feelings. Mentoring junior analysts gives me the same feeling at work.

practice.title: Think it through. Then try it.
practice.intro: I push for the things I want, and I also let some things take their course. Two small stories show both sides.

items.title: The deadline passed. I still asked.
items.text: I have missed a hackathon application deadline and messaged the organizers anyway. When a talk I really wanted to attend put me on the waitlist, I reached out then too. I can’t control the answer, but I can make my interest clear. I would rather ask one more question than decide for myself that the door is already closed.

items.title: My life decision ended in a tie.
items.text: When I had to decide whether to stay or move, I did what an optimization person does: I built a scoring sheet and weighed both options on every dimension I cared about. The totals came out almost the same. So I chose to go with the flow, and I remind myself that everything is unfolding as it should. The scores showed me the trade-offs. Living well with the choice is up to me.

research_hero.title: A second life for useful hardware.
research_hero.lead: Many returned parts still have value. My main research interest is AI-assisted reverse logistics: how to use information about an asset to decide what needs inspection and what should return to inventory, be remarketed, or be scrapped. My industry work is in data center supply chains.
research_hero.scope: The SSADS study uses three synthetic reverse-logistics scenarios. Related papers examine retail forecasting, simulated supply-chain interventions, and LLM-routing assurance.

research_feature.title: Which returned assets deserve an inspection?
research_feature.intro: Returned equipment often arrives with a note and an unknown condition. In SSADS, text readers—including an LLM—turn those notes into condition and signal-quality estimates. Inspection and recovery logic use that evidence under a shared labor budget.
research_feature.finding: In three synthetic scenarios, the keyword implementation improved recovery value over a noisy full-inspection comparator while reducing inspection cost. At equal inspection cost, targeting added value in the aircraft scenario and had little economic effect in the other two settings.
research_feature.boundary: These are benchmark results, not measured savings from a production deployment. A risk-blind policy that skipped inspection scored higher under the benchmark’s purely economic objective.
research_feature.contribution: I proposed the core research idea and methodological framework for SSADS: using semantic signals from return notes to inform inspection and recovery allocation.

research_implementation.title: From a model to a workflow.
research_implementation.intro: For a returned part, the practical question is what should happen next: return it to inventory, remarket it, or scrap it. I think about that decision through three factors.

factors.title: Cost & value
factors.text: Unit cost, expected recovery value, and the effort needed to inspect and process the item.

factors.title: Scarcity & demand
factors.text: How difficult the part is to replace, and whether keeping it available can meet an inventory need.

factors.title: Condition
factors.text: What is known about the item, what the return notes suggest, and what further inspection needs to establish.

research_implementation.goal: My goal is to help teams connect AI-extracted evidence with costs, inventory needs, and feasible recovery routes. SSADS studies one part of that workflow: note-informed inspection and recovery allocation under labor constraints.
research_implementation.invitation: I welcome conversations with teams trying to put these ideas into practice.
